label: early original-phase input of 3/f/e/c/x/d after a sequence starting with a/o/r/n/i/g/k
explanation: Fires only in the original (input) phase, at steps t=1..5 (peaking at t=2-3, about 74% of mass at t=2-3), never at t=0, the delimiter, or the copy phase. The current input is almost always one of 3, f, e, c, x, d (3 has the most, then f and e; together the six hold about 97% of mass), and usually the first time that token appears (91% of mass). Magnitude depends on the earlier context: the strongest activations come when the sequence starts with a/r/o/n (and to a lesser degree i/g/k), e.g. a o [f] [3], a o x [e]. The token set plus position alone has high mass recall (0.96) but low precision (0.16); adding the first-token condition gives dev F1 0.44 (P 0.38, R 0.52, mass recall 0.68). Looks like a graded sum of token identity and early-prefix content rather than a clean boolean, so precision stays limited. It does not fire on other letters (t, u, v, z, s are near zero) or on any step from t=6 on.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: t=1 & prev_tok=x (+5.96), t=1 & prev_tok=e (+5.93), t=1 & prev_tok=f (+5.26), t=1 & prev_tok=3 (+5.09), t=1 & prev_tok=1 (+5.08), orig0=a (+3.65). Lower it: t=6 (-4.22), t=7 (-4.05), orig0=s (-3.88), t=8 (-3.37).
